Question: What would happen if I dyed my hair today then bleached it TMR?
Answer: There is not a soul on this forum who can answer your question. Do it, see what happens and let us know. Why in the world would you diye it one day and then bleach it the next? This makes absolutely no sense whatsoever. If you want a temporarily dye, go buy spray on hair color. Style your hair out the way you want and put some hairspray on it. Then spray the temporary color dye on top, just a little at a time until you get the saturation that you want allowing it to dry in between each application as to not mess up your hairstyle. Then you can go back over and add some more Hairspray. Tomorrow you can shampoo it out.

Question: How do you tell people you don’t cut black hair politely?
Answer: All of us in the industry excel in some areas more than others. The best thing you can do is what I have done in the past with other services that weren't necessarily due to ethnicity as I am sure is the same with you. It isn't your area of expertise and you struggle with getting good results. I've never been really great at flat tops. I'm so glad they're not in Vogue anymore. We had a cutter in our salon who did beautiful flat tops. Anytime I would get someone in my chair who wanted a flat top I would politely say “Karen is our flat top specialist, she does flat tops better than anyone else in the salon. If you wouldn't mind waiting a few minutes I can get you in with her because I want you to love your hair today”. They would always want to wait the extra time to get in with Karen since I gave her such high accolades. This got me off the hook of doing a clumsy inadequate job and at the same time I didn't come off as being a snob that did not want to do their hair. So, if you get someone that has highly textured hair and you're not good at it, you do the same thing I did. You let them know that you have an expert in the salon who does exceptional work with highly textured hair and you want them to love their hair today. That sounds so much better than saying “Oh, I don't do that kind of hair”. As a trainer, know when a stylist says this, they are telling me they don't do that kind of hair because they do not know how to give exceptional service with special techniques. But a client looks at it as someone who doesn't want to do their hair for some personal reason which is generally not a correct assumption.

Question: Can you think of any bizarre or outlandish styles for hair that were popular at some point in history?
Answer: There was a time in Europe when it was fashionable to wear very high hair. The bigger the hair the better. The whiter the hair and skin the better. This was a big flare and popular with the wealthy Elite. The look was supposed to mimic a life of leisure. Anyone with tan skin was considered a poor laborer. Anyone with ultra white skin and hair were considered to be of a Pampered upper class. Styling the hair consisted of putting and securing a bone scaffolding on top of the head. Long hair was then coated in goose fat and wrapped around the scaffolding to create the lofty styles. This would be followed with a healthy powdering with wheat powder. Sometimes the wheat powder was applied with ballasts built into the wall of small powder rooms. This allowed for ladies to not only powder their wigs but powder there skin at the same time. Hence the term Powder Room evolved into eventually becoming a polite way of saying the ladies restroom. Women would have these Contraptions with goose fat coated hair on top of their heads for months. What would happen over time is the goose fst that would go Rancid. Parasites would move into the hair and onto the scalp. Long pins known as hair pins were used to insert into the big styles to scratch the scalp when it became itchy from parasites. Very nasty, and required lots of perfume. But they weren't bathing that much back then. Usually twice a year. Thank goodness the style went out of Vogue. Sadly the reason it went out of Vogue was because of famine in Europe. People were starving and wheat needed to make the powder for the wigs was no longer envogue. People needed food.

Question: Why isn’t the brand HI LIFT hair dye covering my greys? I’m 100% and following the instructions. I’m using 6/00+6/3. I have tried different formulas to try fix this problem. Including adjusting ratios. Should I just go boring 6/00? Will it look flat?
Answer: What brand of color are you using? Hi lift colors do not usually start as dark as a level 6. Hi lift hair color is not designed to COVER Gray hair. It is used to lighten natural hair with less than 50% gray hair mixed in. There is not enough depositing pigment present in the tube/bottle of color to add pigment other than to control warm tones as it gets lighter during the process. So - the question is; Do you want to cover your gray hair or, do you want to lighten your dark hair mixed in with the gray hair? Use hair color for (gray coverage) at a level 6 to get a level 6 with 20 volume developer. Hi lift color only lifts up to 2 levels with 20 volume developer on natural hair. 3 levels with 30 volume and 4 levels with 40 volume. And - if the hair is darker than a level 5 forget using hair color at all to lift, even if it is hi-lift color. It is not aggressive enough to do the job. Another thing to note is hair color will not lift artificial dye from the hair. So if you are re-appying over the top of previously dyed hair, it will not work. One of the most fundamental things taught in Cosmetology school. Color will not lift color. Only bleach or clay lighteners will lift artificial dye.

Question: Can you put permanent dye over color depositing conditioners like keracolor?
Answer: You can. But if I were going to do it and do it right, I would use a really good clarifying shampoo and leave it on your hair a minimum of 10 minutes before rinsing. This is to remove some of the direct dye from the conditioner. Condition your hair, dry your hair completely before applying color all over.
